name: The Echo of the Ward
summary: A pocket the plains tried to carve after the Iron Grief, so that fresh rock could be brought within reach of a body with no spatial law to move it. It exists as the precedent: the carve tore the parent frame, and every survey of that ground has disagreed more sharply ever since.

attributes.host_tier_note: was a pocket inside a three-slot frame; the pocket is gone and the parent frame is scarred where it was
attributes.size_note: zero: the frame no longer encloses anything, and a tear is not a place

seated.why: written at more than the Ward's illegal value, which is why it tore instead of settling

law_composition.read_as: a law pushed past what a held imprint can carry, so the group stopped holding and the outline was left exposed

vacancy_cost.all_three_paid_seats: it spent its one working seat on the only group it needed and none on the three that keep a pocket from being a hole in a world

attributes.why_it_was_attempted: the Iron Grief was an exhaustion problem, and a world with no spatial law cannot grow, open fresh rock or move its own size - so the answer tried was to write spatial law by hand into a hole and carry ore through it
attributes.what_the_attempt_cost: the parent frame's only layer tore along the cut, which is the one place on the plains where two surveys of the same ground disagree by more than the ordinary disagreement, and which is why nobody will hold a claim there
attributes.what_it_taught: that a seat cannot be taken by writing harder. The successful pocket had to be cut from inside by a body already inside the frame, at a value below what tore

name: The First Ward
summary: A pocket cut into the Hollow Baseline that illegally seats four imprints where the parent frame seats three, one of them spatial, so distance is conserved inside it for the first time on the plains. It exists because a warden can pay the fourth seat out of their own body once a period, and inside it a survey agrees with itself.

attributes.host_tier_note: a pocket inside a three-slot frame, so its budget is the parent's by right and its reading is a theft
attributes.size_note: a pocket is smaller than the smallest authored band; it is a hole in a frame, not a frame

seated.why: iron, cut and caged, because ore is what the pocket was made for
a herb bed, deliberately kept thin, because nothing that can be eaten may be grown freely in a stolen frame
the floor, and the reason the warden's own reserve is what pays for the fourth
the fourth seat, and the whole point: distance is conserved, so a survey agrees with itself and a boundary can be walked

law_composition.overspend: four imprints against a three-slot frame, sustained rather than momentary

vacancy_cost.elemental_law: still vacant, so the chamber has no season and its herb bed has to be cut and dried by hand inside a hole nobody else knows the size of
vacancy_cost.temporal_law: still vacant, so nothing inside is dated and the warden's tenure is counted in their own breathing rather than on a post

attributes.life_form_ceiling_reason: life_law at 0.3 is stolen as well, so it licenses the least and not the most
attributes.who_can_enter: anyone the warden admits, and what is for sale is not admission but measurement: a survey taken inside agrees with itself, which has not been true of this ground since anyone started asking
attributes.what_it_costs_the_holder: one period of upkeep is paid out of the warden's body every period, and the reading returns the same number afterwards, so the cost never falls and never shows up as a wound that would heal
attributes.why_it_is_not_echo_of_the_ward: the earlier attempt tore the parent frame because the carve was made from outside. This one was cut from inside, by somebody already holding the frame, which is the only reason the parent still stands

name: The Glazed Margin
summary: A spirit frame with five of its six seats filled and elemental law deliberately left unwritten, on the near side of the immortal border. It exists to answer a practical question: a border with no season in it cannot be given a timetable, so it has to be held by hand all year by people paid to stand on it.

seated.why: hard glazed ground, which is where the name comes from: the rock vitrifies where the border is fought
the seat that makes the border a line and therefore something worth standing on
enough to cross the border and not enough to hold the far side of it
time runs, but nothing cycles: there is no elemental group to make a season out of
enough for a settlement, not enough for a surplus

law_composition.the_spare_slot_is_the_point: six slots is a budget, not an obligation. This frame took five and left the sixth empty on purpose, which is the only thing this setting records of a tier refusing part of its own capacity
law_composition.layer_distribution: one layer, with one seat deliberately unused

vacancy_cost.elemental_law: No season runs anywhere in the frame, and every other spirit frame has one. The pass in its border cannot be scheduled, so it is a doorway that is open whenever anybody is standing in it; fire is combustion rather than a budget; no elemental can be alive here; and a traveller cannot plan a crossing by calendar, only by asking somebody who has watched it lately.

attributes.life_form_ceiling_reason: life_law is seated; elementals are excluded by the vacant elemental seat rather than by the budget
attributes.why_a_commission_exists: a border that cannot be scheduled has to be built and maintained as standing work rather than as a fortification, and the guild that builds thresholds is the only party on the near side good enough to be paid for it
attributes.the_bed_beyond_it: the crossing attempted here was left unmortared when it failed, and the seat-holders who could not pay the upkeep abandoned it - so the border is still crossed one person at a time by whoever offers most for a place to stand

name: The Hollow Baseline
summary: The mortal frame the setting's first tier was paid for: three imprints, physical 1.4, life 0.62 and qi hard on the 0.1 floor, and elemental, spatial and temporal left unwritten. It exists because somebody had to open a world at all and could only afford three seats, and it is still running on that arithmetic - no season, no clock, no distance, no life form but plant and beast.

seated.why: ore needs hardness and weight; this is the group's middle and the only seat that could cage a core
high, because this seat is doing two jobs: it keeps herb_common alive and it is the reason no humanoid is admissible
the floor of 0.1-100, so it is strained rather than absent: a seed germinates and an ironhide bear reaches five, nothing more

law_composition.layer_distribution: one layer, so the surface law list is the whole law set

vacancy_cost.elemental_law: No season runs, so nothing is ever dormant. herb_common regrowth is limited by grazing and by nothing else, which is why a bad grazing year is a medical shortage before it is a hunger. No elemental body can be alive, so the tier yields no elemental resource and a furnace body has no budget to spend into - every discharge it makes is paid in flesh.
vacancy_cost.spatial_law: Distance is not conserved, so no two surveys of the same ground have ever agreed and possession is proven by a marker standing rather than by measuring where it stands. It also makes the 74-unit size a ceiling rather than a range, which is the physical reason this world cannot grow into a spirit world.
vacancy_cost.temporal_law: No clock. The single flood a year is the only cycle the ground offers, so festivals hang off a measured flood post instead of a date, contracts run to the flood, and a settlement on the watercourse is revocable once a generation.

attributes.life_form_ceiling_reason: the single life_law seat is already fully spent keeping plant and beast coherent, so the tier admits no humanoid and no elemental - which is why every practitioner on the Cairn Field is a visitor and why the ring's entire economy is spectators
attributes.ceiling_not_range: 74.0 of a 10.0-100.0 band, and because spatial_law is vacant nothing presses the frame open: it is born at a size and it stays there
attributes.resident_tolerance: a body grown under this composition has no spare groups to fall back on, so a tuned spirit-band practitioner can hold a dantian here for hours and a spirit-tier technique fails at full strength rather than at reduced strength
attributes.what_it_buys: iron for the one craft a mortal body can be trusted with and herb for the one medicine a mortal body can be dosed with, which is the whole of the tier's yield
attributes.why_it_is_cheapest_to_hold: upkeep 0.22 against 7.4 at the top tier; the cheapest frame in the setting is the one that could not afford a fourth seat

name: The Long Count
summary: A mortal frame that spent its third seat on temporal law instead of life law, and paid for a calendar with the ability to be alive: it has perfect timekeeping and no living thing on it. It exists to prove the mortal budget is a choice, and it is why the Debt Line's ledgers are the only exact record anywhere below the Spirit Peaks.

seated.why: enough to work stone and nothing more, because stone was never the point here
the floor, as everywhere mortal, so a body could still have attempted a gate
the mistake: a real clock, exact enough to date a debt to the day

law_composition.the_awful_part: life_law is on the vacant list, and an unwritten law group has no dial at all - so nothing alive can be built out of it. There is no plant, no beast, no herb, no body. The frame is exact and it is empty.

vacancy_cost.life_law: The whole cost. No process runs on it, no substance carries it and no life form is licensed by it, so a world with temporal law and no life law can hold a calendar and nothing else. Nobody can be born here, nothing can be farmed, and a resident cannot eat - which is why every household that could pay to leave did.
vacancy_cost.spatial_law: distance is not conserved even here, so the settlement that governed the frame could not say where its own border was, and the exodus had no way to be counted
vacancy_cost.elemental_law: no season, so a crop could never be planned even by a people who had a clock

attributes.life_form_ceiling_reason: the frame seats no life law at all, so nothing alive is admissible - this is the one mortal world in the setting whose emptiness is not a policy but an absence
attributes.why_it_was_sealed: the households that could afford the stair left first, taking their record-books; the households that could not were sealed in with them, and the sealing was a precaution that turned into the end of the settlement
attributes.what_left_it: the dating conventions. The Debt Line binds a child to a named debt before first breath is drawn cold, and it can only do that because somebody once had a clock accurate enough to make a date worth binding

name: Nine Seats Court
summary: The immortal frame where ten seats sit over six law groups, so four are duplicates and four more can never be filled because there is no seventh group to put in them. It exists because four unfillable high seats produce the only authority this setting can build without filling them: an office that names a seat and may not take one.

seated.why: surface reading, strong enough for the terrace cuts
the first duplicate, and the surplus one the surface cannot carry
held once; above this tier the surface is stable enough not to need it twice
held once, at the reading that funds the tier's five-period upkeep
the second writing, and where a law written twice is strongest
held once; the clock runs five to fifty times slower than a mortal's and that is the discount
held once, and written twice by the ley below the terraces
the duplicate, which is why fire is simply fire on this ground
held once and duplicated, which is the only tier where both a humanoid and an elemental are licensed and neither is scarce
the second writing

vacant: a seventh group, which does not exist
any duplicate of spatial_law or temporal_law, which nobody has wanted
law_composition.layer_distribution: two layers: six imprints on the surface and four on the shelf above it
law_composition.the_four_that_cannot_be_filled: four seats have nothing to hold them, and one attempt to give one of them a seventh law consumed the slot on an absence, after which it cannot be told from an empty one - so the vacancies are vacant rather than merely unfilled

vacancy_cost.an_unfillable_seat: The cost is authority without power. An office here may name a seat and may not take one, and every appointment passes a trial the office cannot judge - so the tier's whole hierarchy is a queue for ground nobody can buy, which is why it is never drained and always crowded.

attributes.life_form_ceiling_reason: the first tier that gathers three groups into one shell, so elementals exist here; and the duplicated life imprint is why a second copy is licensed as easily as the first
attributes.why_it_is_not_any_dao_s_home: the immortal tier is the only tier no Dao is native to, so this is a tier everything passes through rather than one anything belongs to - which is exactly what an office that names a seat and may not take one needs

name: Patient Hold
summary: The top frame: fifteen imprints over three layers, so nine of them are surplus and the surplus is the ground. It exists because it is the only composition with real slack - the only place a law can be held apart from its effect and read - and because its clock runs ten to a hundred times faster than a mortal's.

attributes.upkeep_note: authored maximum is 5.0; a frame held open past its own reading runs on credit, which is the whole mechanism of the Still Point

seated.why: surface
layer two
layer three
surface
layer two
layer three
surface; the only group with enough range to fund a frame this size, held four times over
layer two
layer three
layer three, and close enough to the 100 ceiling that the shore can be pushed past it
the clock that makes a lifetime a unit of measurement
layer two
layer three
surface
layer two
surface, near the top of its 0.0-1.0 range, which is why everything here is coherent and nothing here is quick

law_composition.layer_distribution: six on the surface, five on the second, four on the third - and nine imprints over six groups is surplus, not slack
law_composition.the_slack_that_is_not_slack: nine surplus imprints is a load rather than a resource, so this ground was assembled by merging and never reached. It is not that fifteen seats exceed six laws; it is that nobody holds fifteen imprints at once

vacancy_cost.nothing_is_vacant: Nothing is unwritten, and that is the problem in disguise: at fifteen imprints the frame is so crowded that a technique cannot be isolated from its effects. Reading a law rather than obeying one requires slack, and the only slack in the setting is the surplus - which is also the load.

attributes.life_form_ceiling_reason: life_law near its ceiling, so coherence is high and speed is not available
attributes.the_clock_price: at thirty-four times a mortal's rate, a person does not live to see a contract mature here, which is why the labour that does run at this tier is a standing hum nobody owns
attributes.why_it_is_the_only_door: it is the only frame with enough imprints gathered close enough together to push one past the end of its range, so it is the only place a tear can be forced - and a tear is the only way anything becomes reachable from anywhere

name: Quartermark
summary: A mortal frame that spent its three seats in the worst possible order: physical at 4.2 so the ore cages a core harder than anywhere below the Spirit Peaks, life at 0.09 so almost nothing grows, and qi on the floor. It exists because a world that can hold a body together but cannot feed one is the only mortal ground where a mortal-band breakthrough costs anything, and practitioners pay to be tested there.

seated.why: three times the baseline's reading, and the entire identity of this world: the ground is hard enough that a foundation stage can be refused by it
inside its 0.0-1.0 range but barely above nothing, so plants are stunted, herb_common is thin and the beasts that live on it are small
the same floor as everywhere mortal, which is what makes the comparison fair: the only difference between this frame and a soft one is what the ground does to you

vacancy_cost.elemental_law: no season, so a stunted crop cannot be timed to anything and the lean months are a habit rather than a forecast
vacancy_cost.spatial_law: distance drifts badly enough that the working face moves between visits, so every claim here is held by a standing marker and by whoever is standing near it
vacancy_cost.temporal_law: no clock, so a contract to supply ore has no date and is discharged when the water rises

attributes.life_form_ceiling_reason: life_law at 0.09 is spent keeping plant and beast coherent and there is nothing left over, so the ceiling holds here for the same reason it holds on the plains - only thinner
attributes.the_exported_scarcity: a hungry frame with hard stone: it cannot feed a visitor and it can make a visitor's body fail, which is a service rather than a resource
attributes.why_practitioners_pay_to_come: the plains are a soft frame: a trial held there proves that the body survived ordinary ground. Quartermark refuses the attempt, so a certificate from here is the only one a body can carry back down the stair
attributes.its_own_iron_grief: its seam was spent later than the plains' and is not on any map, because no geography record survived to hold it - the working face was abandoned rather than worked to nothing

name: The Seventh Ward
summary: A name, not a place: the frame somebody tried to build by seating a seventh law in a vacant slot, which cannot work because a slot cannot hold what does not exist. It is kept as a record so the attempt is traceable, and so nobody spends a seat on an absence a second time.

attributes.host_tier_note: attempted against the immortal tier's four unfillable seats; nothing was produced to be located anywhere
attributes.time_flow_note: none observed: a slot consumed by an absence never produced a frame to read

vacant: every group, including the sixth that was already written elsewhere in the attempt
law_composition.what_was_consumed: one of the four vacant seats. The seat was spent holding an absence, and afterwards it cannot be told from an empty one, so the loss is permanent and invisible at the same time

vacancy_cost.the_cost_everybody_pays: The price is not one lost seat. It is that the four unfillable seats above this tier can now never be certified empty, so the ledger at the top of the setting cannot close, and unclaimed capacity is the only thing that pays its own upkeep

attributes.life_form_ceiling_reason: no frame was produced, so there is no ceiling to read
attributes.why_it_is_still_recorded: a name that can be searched is a name that cannot be proposed again, and the practice that grew around the failure - a household marking its own threshold because the world will not guarantee welcome - reads the attempt rather than the outcome
attributes.what_it_is_not: not a destroyed world and not a hidden one. Nothing happened here except that a slot was spent, and the honest record of that is a noun with no coordinates

name: The Surplus Shelf
summary: The second layer of the Nine Seats Court, named separately because its law list is a different list: four imprints, one of each duplicated group, and the only ground in the setting where a law written twice has the second writing win. It exists because anything that must not fail is built here and anything that must fail is built one layer down on purpose.

attributes.host_tier_note: layer two of a two-layer immortal frame; a layer carries its own law list, so it is a frame in its own right
attributes.size_note: its own share of the volume, a fifth of the parent

seated.why: the stronger of the two writings
the stronger of the two writings, and the reason the shelf drifts
the stronger of the two writings
the stronger of the two writings

vacant: any group not already duplicated below
law_composition.layer_distribution: four imprints on four groups, one per duplicated group

vacancy_cost.spatial_and_temporal_absent_here: The shelf has no spatial and no temporal imprint of its own, so it inherits both from the ground below it rather than declaring them. That inheritance is why anything standing here is being measured against four imprints the ground under it does not have, and why nothing that cannot be carried up can be stood on it.

attributes.life_form_ceiling_reason: inherited from the layer below, which is where it is actually written
attributes.the_one_property: a law written twice has the second writing be the stronger one, so this is the only ground in the setting where a law can be bent deliberately - and it is also the only ground where anything standing on it is quietly being compared against a different version of the same six laws
attributes.who_is_excluded: most of what a mortal-band or spirit-band body is, which is why access here is a discipline rather than a journey and the hierarchy below is a queue for it

name: The Cutaway Isle
summary: A spirit-tier isle cut out of the Cloudshelf's floor when a jade seam was worked out from under it, then resealed with the same six groups at drifted readings. It exists because a severed piece keeps its laws and slowly stops agreeing with its parent, and because the drift makes its jade legible at a number nobody ashore can match.

attributes.host_tier_note: severed from a spirit frame and resealed, so its law budget is its parent's six and it holds six
attributes.size_note: an order of magnitude under its own tier's floor, because a cut piece is sized by what was cut out of it

seated.why: drifted a tenth above the parent, so the isle's own stone is measurably harder than the shelf it came from
drifted, so a boundary on the isle can be walked but will not agree with a chart of the parent
drifted high, which is the whole commercial point
drifted slow, so a season on the isle runs out of step with every schedule ashore
drifted low, so nothing elemental grows there
drifted down, which is why the residue life is all low-grade

law_composition.layer_distribution: one layer, resealed rather than grown
law_composition.the_important_number: no group is out of range and none is doubled, so the isle is legal and simply wrong. Its qi reads 4.9 where the parent reads 4.6, and two shores that disagree by three tenths cannot both be right about what a cargo is worth

vacancy_cost.nothing_is_vacant: Nothing is unwritten here either. The cost of severance is drift: every imprint is inside its range and none of them agrees with the frame it was cut from, so every measurement taken on the isle is locally valid and useless as evidence anywhere else

attributes.life_form_ceiling_reason: humanoids are licensed and there are none, because nobody with the means to stay has a reason to
attributes.why_it_was_severed: the jade seam on the shelf ran under the isle's floor, and the only way to reach it was to take the isle out and leave it standing on its own
attributes.why_it_is_dormant_rather_than_dead: it still pays its own upkeep, at a rate nobody collects, which is why a charter over it is worth more than its stone and why somebody is always working the tailings

name: The Held Note
summary: A pocket inside the top frame where fifteen imprints are pressed into one held value of temporal law rather than spread across three layers, so a single act of attention can be sustained past the end of any civilisation that has existed. It is the hidden domain Mind Dao's home tier licenses and nothing else does.

attributes.host_tier_note: a pocket inside the third layer, so the imprints it compresses were already surplus and cost the parent nothing to give up
attributes.size_note: the smallest frame in the setting and the only one where the size band is meaningless, because nothing here is a volume

seated.why: fifteen imprints of every group pressed into one dial at one reading, close to but inside the 100 ceiling, which is the whole mechanism
held separately, because attention has to be fed and the pocket cannot run on the temporal imprint alone

law_composition.layer_distribution: one layer; a pocket is one layer by definition
law_composition.the_impossible_part: four groups are missing and the pocket works anyway, because it never needed a body - it needs an act of attention held past its own natural length, which is the one thing the setting's clock makes expensive rather than impossible

vacancy_cost.four_groups_unwritten: Nothing in here is stone, ground, weather or alive. Everything that survives the hold has to be carried in already coherent, so nothing can be grown, built or born at the far end of it - which is why the practice around this pocket is a hum held by a floor full of people and not a workshop.

attributes.life_form_ceiling_reason: nothing lives here; the pocket is entered by attention and left by attention, and the people who hold the floor outside it are not inside it
attributes.why_it_is_hidden: a frame this crowded is the only condition under which a law can be held apart from its effect and read, and a law that can be read can be answered - so the ground is kept off every chart and the office that tends the floor is not told what is under it
attributes.the_mechanical_content_of_the_still_poin: holding one reading of one group at ninety-six for longer than a civilisation lasts is the entire content of the top tier's era, and the reason the top tier's Dao is the one whose home is here

name: The Matching Shore
summary: Not a place with a composition but the agreement itself: the far side of the one tear that has stood open, named by the single law group both frames write at the same value. It exists to make the rule exact - two frames become reachable only where they agree, and everything else about this world is somebody's claim.

attributes.host_tier_note: reached from the top tier's shore, so it is counted beside that tier; it has no surface of its own to be counted with
attributes.time_flow_note: not measurable from this side: a frame with no temporal imprint has no rate anybody here can observe
attributes.size_note: unmeasurable for the same reason its distance is: spatial_law is not written here, so nothing on this side can report how big it is
attributes.upkeep_note: none, because nothing is being held: this is a fact about an agreement, and an agreement pays nothing

seated.why: the one group written at the same reading on both sides, and the only reason a body can cross at all

law_composition.the_honest_caveat: these five are not unwritten, they are unknown. Nothing on this side of the tear has observed them, and a frame that has never been surveyed cannot be distinguished from a frame that has no such groups - which is the setting's own argument about vacancy, restated at the only place it matters

vacancy_cost.what_cannot_be_done_here: Nothing on this side of the agreement can be checked. A technique brought through either behaves identically whether its group is seated at one reading or is not written at all, so every account of the far side is an account of somebody's tolerance rather than of the frame.

attributes.life_form_ceiling_reason: no life form has ever been observed on this side of the tear, and the absence of an observation is not an absence
attributes.why_the_status_is_disputed: the holders of the near shore have fortified against arrivals for a generation, and every one of them is fortified in the wrong direction: arrivals are cheap, the danger is what arrives, and nobody has any observation of what that is
attributes.what_a_traveller_carries: not power but tolerance. A realm band is a band of one frame's readings, so it is valid across a boundary only over the overlap, and arriving into a different set meets an unwritten group - which fails at full strength rather than at reduced strength

name: The Unwritable Ledger
summary: A spirit frame whose qi was driven past the top of its authored range by the Void Serpent trade, so the group stopped holding and the tear it opened met a world it agreed with on nothing. It exists as the reason there is a paperless people and a carrying culture that abandoned its price list four centuries ago.

attributes.upkeep_state: unpaid; a frame that cannot be held is not closed, it is merely unreachable

seated.why: held
held
held, and it is why people used to live here
held, which is why the settlement kept a calendar nobody else below the peaks could keep
held, and it is where the serpents were kept
OUT OF RANGE. The authored ceiling for qi is 100.0, so this group stopped holding, left its outline exposed, and could not be written back without first bringing it under the ceiling

law_composition.layer_distribution: one layer; nothing holds it together

vacancy_cost.none_were_vacant: Nothing was left unwritten here. The failure is the opposite: a group was driven past the end of its own range, so the process stopped running and the substance stopped carrying anything, and no dial remains to push back

attributes.life_form_ceiling_reason: the license was never withdrawn; there is simply nothing inside the frame to hold it, which is a different failure and is why the place cannot be entered to find out
attributes.why_the_trade_ended: a Void Serpent in quantity was worth more than the ship carrying it, and the settlements that carried them wrote the density into their own books. The value would not fit in any record they kept, so what they abandoned was the ledger, and then the frame itself
attributes.what_the_wall_means: two frames become reachable only where they agree on one group at one value. This one agrees with nothing now, so the tear opens onto a wall, and every holder who has ever reached the far side has built facing the wrong way

name: The Tithe Remainder
summary: The spirit frame that first spent all six of its seats on all six law groups, so nothing in it is merely missing. It exists because a schedule only becomes possible where nothing is absent: a breakthrough here can be timed to a qi tide rather than attempted, and a pass can be given a timetable.

seated.why: enough for folded stone and a hard sea floor
the seat that turns a claim into a line, and the reason a coast holds its shape
the only group with a thousandfold range, and the only one that can fund a tier at all
near the floor on purpose: the cycle runs, and the season is not allowed to be generous about it
low, because a high reading here would put the fire valleys out of reach of anyone who could not afford the trip
the first reading that licenses a humanoid anywhere in the setting

law_composition.layer_distribution: one layer, because six imprints over six groups leaves nothing to put in a second

vacancy_cost.nothing_is_vacant_but_the_budget_is: The cost of a full set is not absence, it is thinness. Six imprints have to cover 100-1000 units, so no single body gathers three groups in one place - which is the mechanical reason an elemental, being three groups in one shell, still cannot exist here and must wait for the next tier.

attributes.life_form_ceiling_reason: life_law is seated and has budget left after the humanoid reading, but the same imprint has no elemental form to license - an elemental needs three groups gathered in one shell and this frame's six seats cannot spare them
first_tier_where: a breakthrough can be scheduled rather than attempted
a border can be surveyed and defended as a line
a season exists, so a pass has a safe window
a person's own lifespan is a measurable discount against the world's clock
attributes.the_density_ceiling_is_here: a maximally dense fixed body stops at realm seventeen in this frame because there is no duplicated group left to open the cavity it needs - a composition result, not a discipline failure
